decision: Win well-matched projects through complete writing, visible launch evidence, clear ownership, optional calls and distinct creative scopes. Keep the four website fees; increase useful page allowances to 8 / 10 / 15 / 20 and reserve more delivery time. Lead with buyer fit and finished outcomes, then show the detailed scope.

public_structure.positioning_copy: A clear website for your next stage. Choose a focused professional site or deeper custom work; get finished writing, a tested inquiry path, clear ownership and optional ongoing help.
public_structure.fit_check: A free written fit check: goal, current website, services, timing and budget range. Reply within one business day with a recommended route or any essential follow-up questions; confirm scope/quote after inputs are complete. An optional 20-minute appointment can replace the written exchange. Allow up to 10 minutes of public-page preparation; this is not a free full audit or speculative design.
public_structure.no_default_popularity_badge: Do not label a plan most popular or promise commercial results without evidence.
choice_rules: Focused: eight pages and an adapted established design. Custom: ten pages, original visual direction, a message brief and up to two related service groups. Business: 15 pages, a researched guide, three service groups and two customer journeys. Signature: 20 pages, two researched guides, up to six service groups, three journeys, two initial concepts and bounded motion. Choose creative and business complexity, then page allowance.
Use Roadmap for uncertainty about an existing website. Use Repair when the exact fixes can already be bounded.
Use Brand & Message Sprint when the offer/positioning decision is the obstacle, not as a mandatory charge before every build.
Use Local Presence Setup for missing or inconsistent foundations. Use Local Search Partnership for a real ongoing content/search program.
Use Care for operation and supplied edits; Website Improvement Partnership for one substantive monthly website output. Local Search Partnership has a different search-led work plan.

Choose Local Search Focus for one page/profile output each month; Local Search Partnership for its larger agreed program. Improvement is a separate website-led priority. All three include their own Brochure Care; never sell duplicate care on the same site.

A client chooses one monthly package for the same site. Care is included in the partnerships; never stack duplicate Care charges. Combine overlapping partnerships only through one consolidated scope and revised fee.
Use Workflow Sprint for one bounded connection between existing tools. Use Custom Systems Discovery when screens, roles, data and integrations need defining before a build.
Storefront Launch is a separate purchase because catalog, checkout and fulfillment testing create work a brochure-site tier does not cover.
public_structure.presentation: Lead with four clear website cards, a short fit sentence, full fee, page allowance, design distinction, writing/search inclusions and timeframe. Mark Custom as “For original design” and Business as “For several services”; avoid invented popularity. Put a concise shared-inclusions checklist and detailed comparison below. Existing-site/local/care work gets a separate route; proposal-only specialties remain secondary.

v4_lessons: Complete calendar, not just build days
Every plan starts from a ready, booked kickoff; normal review time is inside the range.
Writing and SEO mean different things to buyers
Name copy quantities, metadata, local setup, monthly outputs and exclusions separately.
One named owner, weekly project updates and stated acknowledgement targets.
Client-controlled accounts, editable files where applicable, license inventory and demonstrated editing/recovery tasks.
Support names hide very different promises
Care defines monitoring, maintenance, backup coverage, edit limits and incident boundaries by platform.
Visible activity is not proven commercial success
Report completed work and observed signals without attributing every inquiry or revenue change to W&M.
Public prices are not measured profitability
Use complete delivery-hour budgets and validate them with actual projects.
A long menu is not a reason to sell everything
Keep four specialist engagements by proposal and exclude social/ads for now.
evidence_limits: V4's 328-competitor sample was purposive. Its prices are advertised offers, schedules are published estimates, reviews are self-selected and incompletely captured, and search/ad observations are estimates or presence checks. They do not establish a market average, conversion rate, W&M delivery hours, willingness to pay, or a causal formula for success. This proposal uses V4 for scope/process lessons and the owner's self-reported capabilities for feasibility; the new prices and hours are explicit planning judgments. V2 adds eight previously unlisted US providers, all with numeric offers and three with build timelines. This remains a purposive comparison, not a representative price survey. Their public schedules do not establish W&M’s hands-on hours. The owner reports 3–4 complete owner hours for a six-page site; V3 uses larger independent scope budgets, reserves and downside cases rather than treating that estimate as measured evidence.
capability_decisions: Strategy, original website writing, custom design/build, mainstream site platforms, local SEO, measurement, integrations, care and custom systems can enter scoped proposals, based on the owner's answers.

Keep the bounded identity module by proposal, with a sample and independent visual-quality check before its first sale. Assisted creation does not remove responsibility for usable files or provenance.
Website plans may use client-supplied case-study facts and approved statements. New customer interviews are not an included obligation until confirmed.
Existing-tool setup and a simple approved welcome/notification connection can be scoped. Ongoing email campaign strategy/management remains out while marked learning.
No social media services, advertising services or in-person photography/video. The expectation of learning ads in a week does not make those services available today.
Capability answers are the owner's assessment. Build samples and complete delivery records before claiming specialization, repeatable outcomes or mature service levels.
definitions: Marketing page

One agreed URL with a defined audience, purpose and approved outline, using an agreed page type. Home, individual service, about, contact and proof pages count. Write as much or as little as the topic, reader and search intent require. No fixed word cap and no extra charge solely because approved content needs more words. New audiences, topics, research methods, templates or functions are scope changes agreed before work.
Researched practical guide

One buyer question answered through an approved outline, client expertise and bounded desk research, with sources checked and linked. Depth is set by the question rather than word count. It differs from a standard service page by its research and explanatory purpose. Included Business/Signature guides use page slots. A guide in Local Search Partnership consumes its two monthly content/SEO units. No ranking guarantee.
Policy page
Up to three client-approved policy texts can be formatted outside a website plan's marketing-page cap. W&M is not being hired to draft legal policies or determine their adequacy.
Content collection entry

A supplied record placed into an agreed reusable template, such as a project or team member. Collection-entry limits are separate from marketing pages because original writing and unique design are not included for each entry. A separately written entry uses a marketing-page allocation or module.
Simple website graphic
A single supporting diagram, icon arrangement or illustration for an agreed page. Full identity design, complex infographics, 3D and open-ended illustration are separately scoped.
Existing-tool link/embed
Place and style an already-configured supported tool. Creating its service rules, calendars, payment logic, CRM fields or automations is setup work and uses the relevant module/sprint.
Revision round

One compiled feedback list from one approver for the current stage, followed by one implementation pass. Refinement within the agreed direction is included; a different concept, new audience or added functionality is a change request. Correcting a defect is not a paid revision round.
Acceptance
Completion of the named deliverables and written tests, followed by explicit client approval. Silence is not treated as launch permission.
Defect

A delivered item failing the agreed acceptance criteria because of W&M's implementation. Correct it without using a client's monthly output allowance. New preferences, new requirements and subsequent third-party changes are different work.
Complete project hours

Include discovery, research, copy, design, production, QA, calls, messages, revisions, handoff and expected defect correction. Internal hours help price scope; they are not a hidden limit that lets W&M abandon an agreed fixed deliverable.
Writing scope without word caps

Agree the page purpose, topic/question, available evidence, research method, deliverables and review rounds before booking. The agreed research is client facts plus ordinary desk/query research; original interviews, surveys, specialist legal/scientific research or additional topics require a separate scope. W&M absorbs its own underestimation. Extra length required for the unchanged approved purpose does not trigger a fee.
Page-count uplift

Final user choice: Focused 8, Custom 10, Business 15 and Signature 20 at unchanged fees. This supersedes the initial mechanical 20% increase and earlier Business 12 choice. Storefront information pages rise from five to six. Audit samples, maintained-site limits, supplied entries, products and module quantities remain their own scope units.
readiness: Signed scope and initial payment; agreed platform, pages, forms, content types and acceptance checks.
One decision maker with authority to approve copy, visual direction, access and launch.
Business facts, service/product details, permissioned proof, current brand assets and client-approved policy wording.
Domain, hosting/platform and required tool access through client-owned accounts or delegated roles.
Known constraints, dependencies, third-party fees and migration/recovery needs disclosed.
A reserved kickoff date and a target launch range confirmed in writing. An inquiry date or deposit alone is not the start of the delivery clock.
delivery_policies: Readiness and queue

Allow roughly one week for collecting inputs as an initial planning allowance, but do not promise that client-controlled readiness has a fixed duration. State the next available start separately from the plan's active delivery range.
Owner work and elapsed time

The quoted calendar is not a billable-hour claim. Short builds can finish earlier by explicit agreement after every gate passes. Do not promise same-day or four-hour delivery from the owner’s internal estimate. Readiness and the sales queue remain separate from the booked delivery window.
Working calendar

Project weeks are calendar weeks, with work scheduled Monday–Friday, 9am–5pm America/New_York, excluding announced holidays. Project day ranges are business days. Days in a monthly cycle are calendar days of that billing cycle; schedule actual work/reviews on business days.
Feedback

Plan for consolidated feedback within two business days at each gate. Normal review time is included in the planned range; the shortest endpoint requires the prompt approvals stated in that plan. Agree longer review windows before booking.
Weekly update
For active projects, send one weekly update with completed work, preview/evidence, decisions needed, blockers and the next dated milestone. This is included delivery work.
Calls are optional

Written intake, approvals, review and support are the default for every plan/module. All W&M interviews, workshops, sessions, training and walkthroughs elsewhere mean written exchanges plus recorded demonstrations, with the stated appointment available by choice. The appointment substitutes for the corresponding exchange; it does not stack unlimited additional consulting. Provide the same decisions, instructions and acceptance evidence either way. Vendor identity/video verification can still be required by the vendor.
Questions and incidents

Send email or messages through the agreed text channel at any time, including nights/weekends. During active projects, paid monthly service and applicable clarification/defect windows, acknowledge within one business day, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm America/New_York excluding announced holidays. Give the next action and a separate resolution estimate. Care site-down/failed-checkout reports receive triage within one business day. Messages are not continuously monitored; 24/7 submission is not 24/7 staffing, instant response or unlimited new work.
Client delay

Notify the owner when a missing decision threatens a milestone. After five business days beyond the agreed response deadline, issue a pause notice and release the production slot. Resume at the next mutually agreed slot with a new date; do not silently continue charging project labor for waiting.
Change requests

State the requested change, exact deliverable, additional fee and schedule effect. Obtain written agreement before doing it. An internal under-estimate of unchanged agreed scope is W&M's responsibility.
W&M delay

Notify promptly, keep the agreed scope, provide a dated recovery plan and offer the appropriate reschedule/credit/refund for work not delivered. Do not blame the client for an unrecorded internal capacity problem.
Launch control
Launch only after explicit approval and the named acceptance checks. Preserve the agreed rollback path and avoid moving DNS, email or live payments without the owner-approved cutover plan.
Post-launch

For website/store builds, perform an operational check within two business days of launch and again around day 14. The 30-day defect-reporting window starts at launch; a defect reported within it remains W&M's responsibility even if its correction finishes later.
No silent service substitution
If an included tool or platform capability proves unavailable, explain the limitation and agree an equivalent deliverable or revised scope/fee before treating the project as complete.
Monthly cycle completion

All monthly deliverables must finish within the paid billing cycle, including February and other short cycles. Schedule review, QA and reporting on business days by cycle end; a numbered stage never extends the paid cycle automatically.
Daily communication allocation

Reserve acknowledgement and follow-up time each business day inside the delivery/admin budgets. Record actual message, recording and optional appointment time; reforecast returning revisions and support as soon as the reserved allowance is threatened. Keep the accepted deliverable and response standard.
shared_launch_standards: Where these checks apply

Apply the relevant shared checks to every website/store build and to the pages, configurations and journeys changed by Repair, Workflow, monthly production and standalone modules. A module does not include an unrelated whole-site audit. Tests must still cover any shared component it changes.
Content and scope

Reconcile the signed page/form/collection inventory. Check approved business facts, titles, descriptions, headings, links, image alt text and permissioned assets. Verify the client-approved policy texts are present.
Layouts and accessibility checks

Check agreed mobile/desktop widths, keyboard navigation, visible focus, headings, labels, contrast, validation and reduced-motion behavior. Use automated checks plus manual review of essential journeys. Use WCAG 2.2 AA as the design/testing reference; do not call this an independent certification or exhaustive conformance audit.
Browser and journey checks

Test current Chrome and Firefox plus WebKit-based coverage for essential journeys. Record actual versions and any real-device checks; do not label an emulation result as a physical-device test. Verify form receipt and confirmation; for stores, verify the agreed transaction scenarios.
Performance

Agree representative routes and budgets at kickoff. For W&M-controlled pages, propose three desktop and three mobile lab runs per representative page: median FCP ≤1.8s, LCP ≤2.5s, TBT ≤200ms and Speed Index ≤3.4s; worst CLS ≤0.1. Include the homepage and each materially different key page/journey type. Save reports and remedy W&M-controlled failures before launch. Record and pin the runner/browser version, viewport, network/CPU throttling, cache state and test environment; use the same settings for comparison.
Performance limits

Third-party checkout, hosted-platform constraints and vendor scripts must be identified before booking. Any necessary exception needs a specific documented cause, effect and client acceptance; do not silently lower budgets to obtain a pass. Lab runs do not guarantee every real visitor's result or replace field Core Web Vitals, which include INP.
Search foundations

Check indexability/canonicals, sitemap, metadata, relevant structured data and agreed redirects. Verify or submit to Search Console if access is available. These are launch tasks, not a promise of indexing, ranking or traffic.
Measurement

Preserve and test existing agreed tracking on touched journeys where access allows. Custom, Business and Signature include the bounded basic measurement in their scope; Focused includes Search Console access/submission plus existing-tracking checks, not new GA4 installation. M1 is broader measurement work; remove included/reused setup before quoting its incremental fee. Use client-approved consent settings and never send names, emails or form-message text as event parameters.
Ownership and handoff

Deliver account/license inventory, agreed source files, written editing guide with recorded demonstration, recovery responsibilities, tested contact/booking path, outside-cost list and support dates. Verify account access and demonstrate at least one real editing task in the recording; obtain written confirmation that the owner can access the agreed editing workflow. Optional live training is available within the plan allocation.
Completion record

Save scope inventory, approval dates, test versions/results, known accepted limitations, launch/cutover record and support end date. This is evidence of the delivered work rather than a marketing badge.
platform_care: W&M checks the supported code/dependencies and deployment path; retain client-accessible source/build assets and a tested rollback. A custom application/database needs separate support scope.

A supported managed host and compatible maintained plugins are prerequisites. Configure daily file/database backup with agreed retention, stage supported updates, and test a representative restore quarterly. Major upgrades, abandoned plugins and compromise recovery are separately scoped.

The platform maintains its hosted core. W&M checks the site, configured integrations and available version/export recovery. Document what native history/export can and cannot restore before accepting Care; do not promise a complete independent backup when the platform does not support it.

Shopify maintains its core; W&M checks theme/apps, storefront, checkout and notifications. Agree an app/native backup method and its coverage; test theme/catalog recovery in a safe environment. Do not imply that every order/payment/account object can be independently restored.

The client pays and owns hosting, domain, email, plugin/app, integration and backup subscriptions. Record renewal responsibility and escalation contacts. W&M's service fee is separate from these vendor charges.

Quarterly representative recovery tests are included. W&M-caused maintenance regressions are corrected, including necessary rollback, without an extra recovery charge. Unrelated incidents, compromise or data loss receive the stated triage, then a separately approved recovery scope and fee. Client/provider responsibilities and backup alerts are documented at onboarding.
money_and_ownership: Website and store payments

40% to reserve the agreed start, 30% after approval of copy/design direction, and 30% after staging acceptance before the scheduled launch. Show dollar amounts and milestone definitions in the proposal. No production work starts without agreed scope and initial payment.
Finite sprints and discovery
50% at booking and 50% on delivery/acceptance of the agreed output. Local Presence Setup's final milestone is completion of the specified work and handoff, not a platform verification outcome.
Modules

Standalone modules use 50/50 payment; modules added to a build use that build's written milestones. Care onboarding is paid before onboarding starts and must pass eligibility before recurring service begins.
Monthly service

Bill one month in advance on an agreed date. Month-to-month, no annual lock-in. Cancellation received before the next billing date prevents the next renewal; the current paid cycle remains available. Show renewal and cancellation instructions before enrollment.
Unused monthly work

Client-unused edit/output allocations do not accumulate indefinitely. By day 10, flag missing inputs and propose a pre-approved alternative. If no useful work can proceed, agree a pause before the next cycle. If W&M misses an agreed output for its own reasons, the client chooses a dated carry-forward or a proportionate credit/refund for the undelivered portion; do not sell the same output again.
Project cancellation

Use a written reconciliation: pay for completed agreed work and approved nonrecoverable external expenses; return unearned prepaid fees. Define the reconciliation and payment timetable in the proposal instead of calling every deposit nonrefundable. Existing client agreements keep their terms.
Outside costs

List domain, hosting/platform, stock/fonts, apps, payment/integration usage, backup tools and other third-party fees before signing. Prices here are W&M service fees in USD; show any applicable tax separately. No subcontractor or unusual license is assumed free.
Reuse and credits

A prior paid audit/strategy output that genuinely replaces new work reduces the new scope and fee. Show the reused deliverable and corresponding credit in the next proposal. There is no automatic free discovery hidden inside another fee and no stacking of overlapping services.
Accounts

The client owns the domain and business/platform accounts from the beginning where the provider supports it; W&M uses delegated access. Client-owned pre-existing accounts and data are never withheld as a substitute for collecting a disputed invoice.
Deliverables and licenses

Transfer agreed original deliverables and editable source files under the project agreement after the relevant fees are paid. Identify licensed fonts, stock media, open-source components, third-party platform restrictions and AI-assisted assets separately. Do not promise exclusive ownership of licensed or generated material.
Exit

Provide the current account/license/export inventory and agreed source files. Remove delegated access when requested after handoff; explain any platform export limits. A new migration or training beyond the agreed handoff is quoted before work. For Google Business Profile, follow the platform's prompt separation rules.
Replacement modules

When a module replaces included work, quote only the incremental work. For example, a guided form replacing an included ordinary form removes that ordinary form production/testing line from the build estimate before the upgrade fee is agreed. Retain the acceptance tests that still apply.
Module review and defect support

Standalone modules include one consolidated review round unless their scope explicitly includes two. Production/design/setup modules receive handoff and a 30-day defect-reporting window for W&M-delivered work. M9 has its stated 30-day platform follow-up checks, with no guaranteed platform decision; M12 support is named in its quote. Assessment/strategy-only deliverables receive 14 days of clarification and factual correction.
google_profile_rules: For GBP work, obtain authorization and retain client ownership. Disclose in writing and on invoices that Google provides the profile free and W&M charges for its work. Publish the required third-party disclosure link and notify clients of it at onboarding/renewal. Keep GBP reporting separate from other platform metrics. Google requires a way for the client to regain exclusive control within seven business days of a separation notice. Eligibility, verification and platform decisions are not guaranteed.

rules: Initially allow two website projects in active production at once, plus up to two waiting for a specific client decision. This is an initial operating limit, not a measured maximum. A returning review must have reserved hours before another start is accepted.

Start at most two new website projects per week during the first three completed website pilots; custom projects may require a lower cadence. Raise the ceiling or reduce reserves only after three complete website time logs through their 30-day defect windows and evidence of on-time delivery, using the next eight-week phase calendar. Reforecast immediately after the first material overrun; do not wait for three jobs to protect existing commitments.

Keep all calls, revisions, testing, post-launch support and recurring work within the 32 delivery hours/week. Initially reserve at most eight of those hours/week for recurring work; the remaining project allocation is not automatically sold out.

Reserve 14 owner hours for Focused, 17.5 for Custom, 32.5 for Business and 51.25 for Signature initially. Assign hours to actual writing/review/launch weeks, including post-launch checks and defect work; calendar ranges do not spread peak work automatically.
Keep five weekly reserve hours unsold for interruptions beyond per-project allowances. Do not promise capacity based on working more than the stated 50-hour business week.
Check a dated eight-week calendar before accepting each start. If peak commitments exceed 32 hours, change the new start/scope or fund qualified help before booking; preserve already accepted work.

Stagger quarterly restore tests and explicitly reserve returning reviews, launch checks, day-2/day-14 checks and support in dated weeks. There is no revenue target supplied and demand is unknown. Do not turn “as many clients as I can get” into unlimited support, unlimited parallel builds, or a forecast of full utilization.

Record AI/Semrush subscription and usage costs, payment fees, client-paid subscriptions and general overhead separately. Before a monthly technical fix is agreed, identify its exact URLs/components, review and acceptance tests; split or separately quote larger work before commitment.

The dated 32-hour delivery limit controls every new booking and overrides the two-start ceiling. Two complete Focused reservations (28 hours) plus the maximum recurring allocation (8 hours) would total 36 hours, so their production/review/launch work must be staggered or new starts reduced. The five-hour whole-business reserve stays unsold.

scenarios.name: Two focused projects in a month
scenarios.explanation: A demand illustration: two Focused projects completed in a month and two optional Care clients. It is not a claim that these clients will be won.

scenarios.name: A mixed midrange month
scenarios.explanation: Two Focused sites, one Custom site, two standalone Care clients and one Local Search Focus client. The search client already has Care included.

scenarios.name: A higher-end month
scenarios.explanation: One Business completion per month and one Signature completion every two months, plus the stated recurring clients. Fractional completions are steady-state averages; milestone cash receipts vary.

capacity.scenario_limit: These are illustrative steady-state averages for capacity planning, not sales forecasts or monthly cash-flow promises. Payment milestones make actual cash receipts uneven. Demand, sales conversion, cancellations and actual delivery time remain unmeasured.

pilot_rollout: Finalize the scope sheet, payment/ownership terms, intake form, approved platforms, source/license handling and acceptance templates. Build the matching samples listed below.

Present the two website groups and four distinct options, plus Care, Roadmap and Repair. Offer Local Search Focus/Partnership when the existing sample and access requirements are met. Keep specialties by proposal; do not present 15 equal homepage cards.
First three complete deliveries/cycles per offer

Log all owner hours through post-launch support, unattended AI runtime, client delays, revision causes, actual tool costs and completion evidence. Use these observations to revise hours, booking limits and public timelines.
Inspect lead quality, fit calls, proposal reasons won/lost, and hours already spent. Fix scope misunderstandings before changing prices solely because one prospect objected.
Compare completed jobs/cycles with the planned price/hours. Adjust forward-looking scope, price or timing when the evidence warrants it; do not reduce existing signed entitlements.
Choose the few services worth promoting most, based on delivery quality, effective rate, demand and owner preference. Continue, narrow or retire low-fit offers.

Revisit only after the owner explicitly confirms readiness and a real sample, tracking process, scope, price and support model are reviewed. No automatic activation in a week and no scheduled commitment created here.
proof_pack: A sample Roadmap with screenshots, affected URLs and a prioritized decision.
A custom website example with original copy, mobile/desktop views and a completed inquiry test.
A launch acceptance checklist and a real handoff/account inventory.
A monthly Care report with a recorded restore/rollback demonstration.
A monthly Improvement example showing the actual changed page and acceptance check.
For local work: a permissioned profile-change log, neutral review-request process and report distinguishing work from outcomes.
For stores/workflows: representative transaction/exception tests and operator training examples.
For identity: usable vector exports and a quality-reviewed example before promoting the module.

Focused design-system sample: show the actual established visual direction, one completed eight-page sample, an audit record and the comparison with original custom design before selling the faster path. Do not describe reuse as original bespoke art direction.
proposal_template: Client, business problem, intended result and selected plan.
Deliverables, exclusions, client inputs, named approver and acceptance tests.
Ready-kickoff checklist, booked start, milestone dates, review windows and target completion range.
Total service fee, milestone amounts, approved outside costs and recurring charges.
Change, pause, cancellation, missed-delivery and unused-allocation terms.
Account/file ownership, licenses, editing and recovery responsibilities.
Support coverage, response targets, defect window and exit/handoff.
Explicit approval to begin; separate explicit approval to launch.
panel_standard: Three independent Astra judges review the exact current V3 catalog, policies, buyer-preview source and competitive decision record; delivery also reviews economics. Every one of 15 plans and 13 modules needs an explicit verdict. Resolve material blockers and rebind all changed files before unanimous approval. Approval is for a controlled pilot design, not proven conversion, profitability or delivery performance.
future_website_change: This is a planning deliverable. It does not publish these prices or replace live packages. After the owner chooses the plan architecture, update the offer catalog, pricing cards, service pages, FAQs, intake, proposal/payment templates, support terms and downloadable scope sheets together; preserve existing accepted commitments.
v2_changes: User-selected final allowances: Focused 8, Custom 10, Business 15 and Signature 20. These supersede the earlier smaller draft; Storefront information pages increase to 6.
No website-copy word caps. Scope by topic, evidence, research method, approved outline and review rounds.
Email/text anytime, acknowledgement within one business day during the published business calendar; all W&M calls optional.
Explicit query/page mapping, original writing, technical search foundations, tested forms, editing guide, launch evidence and next-90-days recommendations.
Keep $2,950 / $4,500 / $7,500 / $11,500; increase reserved hours to 14 / 17.5 / 32.5 / 51.25. Verify real margins and demand through paid pilots.
A dedicated customer-facing preview, clearer upgrade reasons, written recommendation CTA and evidence-qualified competitor comparison.
Basic GA4/Search Console and one tested primary inquiry event in Custom and above. Advanced tracking/dashboard work remains separately scoped, with no duplicate charge.
ai_delivery: Research collection, structured analysis, copy drafts, component assembly, setup assistance and repeatable tests. Human attention still verifies facts, design, permissions, tool outcomes and completion.

Record owner hands-on time, unattended AI/tool runtime, client waiting and queue delay separately. Calendar promises include the agreed review windows; concurrent AI runs do not create unlimited review capacity.

Use only authorized, necessary client data in approved tools. Do not upload passwords, private customer records or confidential source material without the appropriate authorization and handling arrangements. Keep claims, rights/licenses and production changes subject to review.
Describe the outcome and quality checks honestly. Do not claim every line or image is hand-made; explain AI assistance when relevant to client consent, rights, confidentiality or the agreed process.
No faster plan skips factual approval, browser/form checks, rollback planning, explicit launch approval, ownership handoff or its included defect support.
profit_strategy: Sell original writing, design fit, clear services, search foundations, tested customer actions and ownership. Do not reduce the sales page to dollars per page.

Use Custom for buyers seeking original design with one main journey; Business when several service groups need two distinct paths. Retain Focused for a clear straightforward need, and Signature for the deeper portfolio it actually serves.

Show actual Focused/custom examples, page-map examples, a short editing demo and a redacted launch checklist. Label concept samples as concepts; use testimonials or outcome numbers only with evidence and permission.

Record all delivery/support hours and actual costs by offer; maintain a dated capacity calendar. Remove low-value work or revise future pricing if reserves fail. Never cut a signed deliverable because internal time runs over.
Offer optional Care, Improvement or Local Search only for a stated ongoing need. Include Care once. Recommend one monthly route, disclose outside costs and avoid forced subscriptions.

Track inquiry source, qualified written recommendations, quotes, acceptance rate, average project value, realized contribution per owner hour, revision time and support load. Review after five qualified proposals and three complete deliveries per offer; small samples are directional.
Test one change at a time

Compare the offer explanation or CTA while holding scope/price stable. Change future prices only when qualified demand, won/lost reasons and actual delivery cost support it. Revenue scenarios are not sales forecasts.

Eight makes Focused’s allowance visibly larger than Signal Grove’s published 5–7-page entry. Ten matches Cerulean’s published count, while W&M remains more expensive and must substantiate its original design/research scope. Fifteen matches Sprout at $7,500; this removes a quantity objection but does not establish overall superiority. Twenty remains a substantial Signature allowance. These are tested offer hypotheses, not statistically optimal counts.
